close_reason: Closed as workspace policy observation. The hybrid re-export pattern (top-level + module alias) is canonical workspace practice — mirrors jmap-calendars-types::jscalendar. Adopting a stability contract is a workspace-wide policy decision filed as JMAP-84zs (P3): document the re-export stability contract in workspace AGENTS.md and decide on version-pin tightness at crates.io release time. No per-crate change needed.
description:
The diff added two pub-use surfaces from jmap-jscontact-types
(lib.rs lines 78, 91-96):

1. Module alias:
   ```rust
   pub use jmap_jscontact_types as jscontact;
   ```
   Exposes the entire upstream crate as `jmap_contacts_types::jscontact::*`.

2. Top-level re-exports of 30+ types:
   ```rust
   pub use jmap_jscontact_types::{
       Address, AddressComponent, Anniversary, AnniversaryDate, Author,
       Calendar, CryptoKey, Directory, EmailAddress, JsContactId,
       LanguagePref, Link, Media, Name, NameComponent, Nickname, Note,
       OnlineService, OrgUnit, Organization, PartialDate, PersonalInfo,
       Phone, Pronouns, Relation, SchedulingAddress, SpeakToAs,
       Timestamp, Title,
   };
   ```

Both surfaces commit jmap-contacts-types to forward every breaking
change in jmap-jscontact-types to its own consumers:

- If jscontact-types renames `Name` → `JsContactName`, contacts-types
  breaks.
- If jscontact-types adds a non-default field to any of these types,
  match-arm exhaustiveness in downstream code breaks (#[non_exhaustive]
  mitigates struct construction breakage but not match/destructure).
- If jscontact-types cuts a major version (0.x → 0.y) under semver,
  all callers of contacts-types must update too.

The Cargo.toml dep is `jmap-jscontact-types = { workspace = true }`,
so within the workspace this is fine — the workspace pins both crates
together. But once contacts-types is published to crates.io, the
re-exports become a public commitment. Adding to or removing from the
re-export list is itself a breaking change.

Additional name-collision footgun: the re-export includes common names
(`Calendar`, `Address`, `Name`, `Phone`, `Organization`, `Title`,
`Note`, `Author`). A downstream that depends on both contacts-types
AND calendars-types (a plausible mail-suite consumer) and writes
`use jmap_contacts_types::*; use jmap_calendars_types::*;` gets a
glob-import conflict on `Calendar` (RFC 9553 §2.4 vs the JMAP
CalendarObject). Glob-use is discouraged in practice, but the conflict
is real.

Missing safeguards:
1. No `#[doc(hidden)]` on the re-exports to defer stability.
2. No `serde-jscontact` Cargo feature gating the re-exports, so callers
   cannot opt for the leaner surface.
3. No rustdoc clause on either pub-use block documenting the
   version-lockstep risk.
4. No CHANGELOG entry pinning jmap-jscontact-types to a specific minor
   range.

Recommendation: leave the re-exports for ergonomic parity (callers
genuinely want `jmap_contacts_types::Name`), but:

- Add a rustdoc clause on each re-export block documenting the
  version-coupling.
- Consider gating behind a `jscontact-reexports` feature for v0.x
  callers who want to pin a narrower API surface.
- Document the lockstep relationship in PLAN.md or AGENTS.md.

Cross-reference: AGENTS.md §"Sloppy-Value pattern" and §"hybrid typed
sub-types via jscalendar/jscontact aliases".

Sibling parity: jmap-calendars-types follows the same re-export pattern
(per workspace AGENTS.md). If this finding lands as a doc-clause
addition, it should propagate to jmap-calendars-types as well.
title: Re-exporting 30+ types from jmap-jscontact-types locks public API to upstream with no stability contract
